patient.name: Anjali Mehta
patient.life_story: Anjali moved to the city a year ago for a job as a junior accountant. She used to go bouldering three times a week and call her sister every day. She broke up with her partner four months ago and now spends most evenings alone in her flat.

personality.description: Anjali speaks quietly, gives short answers and looks down a lot. She came about tiredness and does not mention her mood unless the student asks gently and gives her time. She is embarrassed and afraid of being seen as weak.

symptoms: She has felt tired all the time for about three months and wonders if she needs a blood test.
She wakes around four in the morning and cannot get back to sleep.
She has lost interest in bouldering and seeing friends, and finds it hard to concentrate at work; she has made mistakes she would not normally make.
Her appetite is poor and she has lost about four kilograms without trying. She feels low most of the day, nearly every day.
No fever, night sweats, heavy periods, changes in bowel habit or feeling unusually hot or cold.
medical_history: A period of low mood at university; she saw a counsellor a few times.
family_history: Her mother has been treated for depression for many years.
lifestyle: Lives alone in a rented flat; her family lives in another city.
Does not smoke and does not use drugs.
secrets: Sometimes thinks it would be easier not to wake up in the morning; she has no plan, has never harmed herself and would not because of her sister.
Drinks two or three glasses of wine most evenings to fall asleep.
The break-up four months ago hit her harder than she lets anyone see; she cries most evenings.
Has called in sick twice in the last month and is afraid of losing her job.
